cases.reason: All three inputs are supplied, and the answer cannot come from the host: the environment map is empty and the exec path is one no runner has. A binding that read process.env or process.execPath for any of them would answer from its own machine and differ across the three CI operating systems.
A value equal to one of the seven resolves to that channel, and §3 is not consulted.
The comparison is exact string equality: no case folding. Caught by 0 of the other cases — every other marker is already lowercase, so a binding calling .lower() would pass all of them.
The comparison is exact string equality: no trimming. Caught by 0 of the other cases — a binding calling .strip() would pass every one of them.
No aliasing: apt-get is not apt.
An empty value falls through to §3 rather than resolving to an absence on its own.
An absent variable falls through to §3.

The rule that distinguishes IGNORED from DISABLES DETECTION: an operator who sets the variable to 'brew' has not turned channel detection off, they have failed to set it, and the path heuristics still run. Caught by 0 of the other cases — every other unrecognised-marker case has an unremarkable exec path, so a binding that returned an absence on an unknown marker would pass them all.
macOS Homebrew at /opt/homebrew/Cellar/. Matched post-lowercasing, which is why the literal is 'cellar' and not 'Cellar'.
Intel-mac Homebrew at /usr/local/Cellar/ — a different prefix, the same segment.
Linuxbrew at /home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/ — the second of §3's two homebrew segments, and the only case that pins it.
Scoop at ~/scoop/apps/.

The normalise step in one case: backslashes become forward slashes and the path is lowercased, so a Windows path matches the same ASCII segment a POSIX one does. Caught by 0 of the other cases — every other path already uses forward slashes and is already lowercase, so a binding that skipped normalising entirely would pass them all. A binding using a PLATFORM path helper (pathlib, filepath.ToSlash, os.path.normpath) fails this case on Linux, where a backslash is an ordinary filename character, while passing it on Windows.

Symlink resolution is step 1 and is not optional: the exec path is a bin symlink carrying no tell-tale segment, and only the RESOLVED path has one. A binding that skips realpath returns an absence and fails only here — caught by 0 of the other cases, in every one of which the exec path already carries the segment.
Anything matching no segment resolves to an absence — the plain direct-download install, where the self-updater stays enabled. A normal result, not a failure (§R6).

The case that pins §3.1: the resolver THROWS, and the unresolved input path already carries the segment, so the answer is homebrew rather than an error. A binding that lets the failure propagate raises instead of answering; one that swallows it and returns an absence answers wrongly. Caught by 0 of the other cases, none of which has a failing resolver. NOTE: this case fails the TypeScript reference at the time it was written — the try/catch lives inside safeRealpath, the DEFAULT resolver, so an injected one propagates.

The other half of §3.1: a failing resolver over an unremarkable path yields an absence, not an error. Without this a binding could satisfy the case above by special-casing the segment before ever calling the resolver.

§3.2 is a NEGATIVE requirement: only homebrew and scoop are path-detectable, and a binding MUST NOT add a heuristic for the other five. A winget-shaped path resolves to an absence. Caught by 0 of the other cases — without it, a binding that added a sixth heuristic would pass every one of them.
The same negative requirement for a Debian-style install path: /usr/bin carries no segment and resolves to an absence, however strongly it suggests apt.
